Strictly speaking, (9.24) applies only to deviations around the steady state and not to money supply processes that include deterministic trends. However, it is very common to specify (9.20) and (9.21), which were used to derive (9.24), in terms of the log levels of the variables, perhaps adding a constant to represent steady-state levels. The advantage of interpreting (9.24) as holding for the log levels of the variables is that one can then use it to analyze shifts in the trend growth paths of the nominal money supplies, rather than just deviations around the trend.
